eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Diabetes diagnosis and insulin therapy
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have had a diagnosis of either: [1a] T1DM based on the World Health Organization (WHO) diagnostic criteria, and have been on the following daily insulin therapy for at least 1 year: [A] multiple daily injection of long_acting insulin analog (either insulin glargine [U_100 or U_300] or insulin degludec [U_100]) and rapid_acting insulin analog (insulin lispro, insulin aspart, or insulin glulisine), or [B] continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII); Or [1b] T2DM based on the WHO diagnostic criteria, and have received the following daily insulin therapy with or without oral anti_hyperglycemic medications (OAMs) for at least 1 year: [A] insulin: long_acting insulin analog (either insulin glargine [U_100 or U_300] or insulin degludec [U_100]) alone, or in combination with rapid_acting insulin analog (insulin lispro, insulin aspart, or insulin glulisine) or CSII; [B] OAM: up to 3 of the following OAMs in accordance with local regulations: metformin, dipeptidyl peptidase_4 inhibitor, sodium glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, sulfonylurea (should not be more than half of maximum approved doses), glinides, alpha_glucosidase inhibitor, or thiazolidine

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Male contraception agreement
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: male patients: agree to use an effective method of contraception for the duration of the study and for 28 days following the last study treatment

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Female contraception and pregnancy requirements
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: female patients: [3a] women of childbearing potential who are abstinent (if this is complete abstinence, as their preferred and usual lifestyle) or in a same sex relationship (as part of their preferred and usual lifestyle) must agree to either remain abstinent or stay in a same sex relationship without sexual relationships with males. Periodic abstinence (eg, calendar, ovulation, symptothermal, post_ovulation methods), declaration of abstinence just for the duration of a trial, and withdrawal are not acceptable methods of contraception. [3b] otherwise, women of childbearing potential participating must agree to use one highly effective method (less than 1% failure rate) of contraception, or a combination of 2 effective methods of contraception for the entirety of the study. [A] women of childbearing potential participating must test negative for pregnancy prior to initiation of treatment as indicated by a negative serum pregnancy test at the screening visit followed by a negative urine pregnancy test within 24 hours prior to exposure. [B] either one highly effective method of contraception or a combination of 2 effective methods of contraception will be used. The patient may choose to use a double barrier method of contraception. Barrier protection methods without concomitant use of a spermicide are not a reliable or acceptable method. Thus, each barrier method must include use of a spermicide. It should be noted that the use of male and female condoms as a double barrier method is not considered acceptable due to the high failure rate when these methods are combined. [3c] women not of childbearing potential may participate, and include those who are: [A] infertile due to surgical sterilization (hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, or tubal ligation), congenital anomaly such as mullerian agenesis; Or [B] postmenopausal, defined as either: [i] a woman at least 50 years of age with an intact uterus, not on hormone therapy, who has had either: [a] cessation of menses for at least 1 year, or [b] at least 6 months of spontaneous amenorrhea with a follicle_stimulating hormone >40 mIU/mL; or [ii] a woman 55 or older not on hormone therapy, who has had at least 6 months of spontaneous amenorrhea, or [iii] a woman at least 55 years of age with a diagnosis of menopause prior to starting hormone replacement therapy

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Age range
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are between 18 and 64 years old for T1DM, or between 20 and 70 years old for T2DM at the time of informed consent

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Body mass index
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a body mass index of 18.5 to 30.0 kg/m2 for T1DM, or 18.5 to 35.0 kg/m2 for T2DM at the time of screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Hemoglobin A1c value
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a hemoglobin A1c value ≤10% at the time of screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Clinical laboratory test results
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have clinical laboratory test results within normal reference range (except for glycemic parameters) for the population or investigative site, or results with acceptable deviations that are judged to be not clinically significant by the investigator

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Venous access
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have venous access sufficient to allow for blood sampling and administration of insulin for IV administration as per the protocol

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Reliability and availability
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are reliable and willing to make themselves available for the duration of the study and are willing to follow study procedures

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Informed consent
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are able and willing to give signed informed consent

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Investigative site personnel exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are investigative site personnel directly affiliated with this study and their immediate families. Immediate family is defined as a spouse, biological or legal guardian, child, or sibling

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Lilly employees exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are Lilly employees

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Current clinical trial enrollment exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are currently enrolled in a clinical trial involving an investigational product or any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Recent investigational product participation exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have participated, within the last 4 months, in a clinical trial involving an investigational product. If the previous investigational product has a long half_life, 4 months or 5 half_lives (whichever is longer) should have passed from the last dose of investigational product

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Prior LY900018 study participation exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have previously completed or withdrawn from this study or any other study investigating LY900018, and have previously received LY900018

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Known allergies or sensitivity exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have known allergies or sensitivity to LY900018, glucagon, related compounds, or any components of the formulation, or history of significant atopy

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: ECG abnormality exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have an abnormality in the 12_lead ECG that, in the opinion of the investigator, increases the risks associated with participating in the study

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Unstable insulin regimen or blood glucose control exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: any significant changes in insulin regimen and/or unstable blood glucose control within the past 3 months prior to screening as assessed by the investigator

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: High total daily insulin dose exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have received a total daily dose of insulin >1.2 U/kg at the time of screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Poorly controlled hypertension exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have poorly controlled hypertension (ie, supine systolic BP >165 mm Hg or supine diastolic BP >95 mm Hg) at screening, or a change in antihypertensive medications within 30 days prior to screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Pheochromocytoma or insulinoma history exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history of pheochromocytoma (ie, adrenal gland tumor) or insulinoma

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Severe hypoglycemia or loss of consciousness history exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history of an episode of severe hypoglycemia (as defined by an episode that required third party assistance for treatment) in the 1 month prior to screening or have a history of loss of consciousness within the last 2 years induced other than by hypoglycemia

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Epilepsy or seizure disorder exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history of epilepsy or seizure disorder

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Significant medical disorders exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have a history or presence of cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine (apart from T1DM or T2DM), hematological, or neurological disorders capable of significantly altering the absorption, metabolism, or elimination of drugs; of constituting a risk when taking the investigational product; or of interfering with the interpretation of data

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Psychiatric disorders exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have known or ongoing psychiatric disorders that, in the opinion of the investigator, may preclude the patient from following and completing the protocol

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Drug abuse exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: regularly use known drugs of abuse and/or show positive findings on urinary drug screening

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: HIV infection exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection and/or positive HIV antibodies and/or antigen

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Hepatitis C exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of hepatitis C and/or positive hepatitis C antibody

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Hepatitis B exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of hepatitis B and/or positive hepatitis B surface antigen

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Syphilis exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: show evidence of syphilis and/or are positive for syphilis test

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Lactating women exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: are women who are lactating

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Prohibited medications exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: use of daily systemic beta_blocker, indomethacin, warfarin, anticholinergic drugs

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Blood donation exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have donated 400 mL or more blood in the last 12 weeks (males) or in the last 16 weeks (females), or any blood donation (including apheresis) within the last 4 weeks, or total volume of blood donation within 12 months is 1200 mL (males)/800 mL (females) or more at screening

arms.name: LY900018 (Nasal Glucagon)
arms.description: Single 3_mg dose of nasal glucagon (LY900018) administered intranasally by study site personnel during one of the two crossover periods

arms.name: IMG (Intramuscular Glucagon)
arms.description: Single 1_mg dose of intramuscular glucagon (GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered by IM injection by study site personnel during one of the two crossover periods

objectives.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
objectives.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non_inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin_induced hypoglycemia using a non_inferiority margin of 10%

endpoints.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint _ Treatment Success
endpoints.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

objectives.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
objectives.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

endpoints.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Endpoint
endpoints.text: SAE, TEAEs (including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non_nasal AEs), vital signs

objectives.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
objectives.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

endpoints.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Endpoint
endpoints.text: PK parameters include AUC, Cmax, Tmax

objectives.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
objectives.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

endpoints.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Endpoint
endpoints.text: PD parameters include BGmax and Tmax

estimands.name: Primary Efficacy Estimand _ Treatment Success Non_Inferiority
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) or type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) experiencing insulin_induced hypoglycemia who meet eligibility criteria (Per_Protocol Completers Population (at least 66 patients completing both periods with evaluable primary outcome)) Summary measure: Difference in proportions (percentage of patients achieving treatment success: IMG minus LY900018) with a 2_sided 95% confidence interval based on the 1_sample mean of paired differences; non_inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non_inferiority margin of 10%.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of both periods
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues from the study before completing both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason (e.g., withdrawal of consent, adverse event, protocol deviation)

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional treatments to increase plasma glucose
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives additional treatments to increase plasma glucose within 30 minutes after glucagon administration, which is incorporated into the definition of treatment failure (i.e., treatment success requires no additional glucose_raising interventions)

intercurrentEvents.name: Failure to achieve insulin_induced hypoglycemia nadir
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not achieve the required plasma glucose nadir during the insulin_induced hypoglycemia procedure, resulting in non_evaluable primary outcome data

intercurrentEvents.name: Device or administration failure
intercurrentEvents.text: Failure of nasal glucagon device or inability to administer the assigned study treatment as per protocol (e.g., nasal device malfunction, inability to complete IM injection)

estimands.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Estimand
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with T1DM or T2DM who received at least one dose of study treatment (LY900018 or IMG) (Safety Population (all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment)) Summary measure: Frequency and percentage of patients experiencing SAEs and TEAEs by system organ class and preferred term; descriptive statistics for vital signs.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation due to adverse event
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues study participation due to an adverse event prior to completion of the follow_up visit

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of concomitant medications affecting safety assessments
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives concomitant medications that may confound the interpretation of adverse events or vital sign measurements

estimands.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand
estimands.populationSummary: Japanese patients with T1DM or T2DM who received at least one dose of study treatment and have evaluable PK samples (PK Analysis Population (all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment with evaluable pharmacokinetic data)) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean) for AUC and Cmax; median and range for Tmax; geometric mean ratios with 90% confidence intervals for AUC and Cmax comparisons between treatments.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or non_evaluable PK samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing or non_evaluable pharmacokinetic blood samples due to sampling errors, hemolysis, or other technical issues resulting in incomplete PK profiles

intercurrentEvents.name: Vomiting shortly after nasal glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient vomits shortly after nasal glucagon administration potentially affecting systemic absorption and PK profile

Note to Regulatory Authorities: This document may contain protected personal data and/or commercially confidential information exempt from public disclosure. Eli Lilly and Company requests consultation regarding release/redaction prior to any public release. In the United States, this document is subject to Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Exemption 4 and may not be reproduced or otherwise disseminated without the written approval of Eli Lilly and Company or its subsidiaries.

Unless otherwise stated in subsections below, all samples collected for specified laboratory tests will be destroyed within 60 days of receipt of confirmed test results. Certain samples may be retained for a longer period, if necessary, to comply with applicable laws, regulations, or laboratory certification standards.
If a patient sneezes immediately after administration, document using the Nasal and Non_nasal Score Questionnaire (see Appendix 6 for a copy of the questionnaire).

Although all AEs are recorded in the CRF after signing informed consent, SAE reporting to the sponsor begins after the patient has signed informed consent and has received investigational product. However, if an SAE occurs after signing informed consent, but prior to receiving investigational product, AND is considered reasonably possibly related to a study procedure then it MUST be reported.

Pregnancy (maternal or paternal exposure to investigational product) does not meet the definition of an AE. However, to fulfill regulatory requirements any pregnancy should be reported following the SAE process to collect data on the outcome for both mother and fetus.

Nonserious AEs obtained through the questionnaire are recorded and analyzed separately. Only SAEs elicited through the Nasal and Non_nasal Score Questionnaire and Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale are to be recorded as AEs via CRF and reported to Lilly or its designee within 24 hours as SAEs.

If a hypoglycemic event meets the criteria of severe, it needs to be recorded as serious in the CRF (that is, recorded as an SAE). In the case of a hypoglycemic event (other than severe), the actual glucose value, if measured, should be recorded in the CRF, with any treatments administered, and not be recorded as an AE.
Cases of hypoglycemia may be treated with foods rich in carbohydrate such as fruit, juice, skimmed milk, or energy bars.

If the target bedside PG level cannot be achieved within 4 hours after the start of insulin infusion, the hypoglycemia induction procedure will be terminated before glucagon administration, and the patient may have a carbohydrate_rich meal and be discharged from the CRU after medical assessment. Additional safety assessments may be conducted at the investigator's discretion. The patient may be rescheduled for a new dosing visit 1 to 7 days later.

Unscheduled orthostatic vital signs should be assessed, if possible, during any AE of dizziness or posture_induced symptoms. If orthostatic measurements are required, patients should be supine for at least 5 minutes and stand for at least 2 minutes. If the patient feels unable to stand, supine vital signs only will be recorded.
Single ECGs will be collected and stored locally at the investigator's site. Triplicate ECGs will be electronically transmitted to a central ECG laboratory designated by Lilly.

studyInterventions.name: LY900018
studyInterventions.description: Nasal glucagon powder formulation for rescue treatment of insulin_induced hypoglycemia; synthetic single_chain 29_amino_acid polypeptide identical to human glucagon, delivered via single_use nasal dosing device

studyInterventions.name: GlucaGen (Intramuscular Glucagon)
studyInterventions.description: Intramuscular glucagon (GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S); lyophilized glucagon powder requiring reconstitution prior to IM injection; approved product for rescue treatment of hypoglycemia in Japan

studyInterventions.name: Human Regular Insulin (IV)
studyInterventions.description: Diluted human regular insulin (0.3 U/mL, prepared by diluting 15 U human regular insulin [100 U/mL] into 50 mL saline) administered by IV infusion to induce hypoglycemia during the study procedure

studyInterventions.name: Intravenous Glucose
studyInterventions.description: IV glucose administered if patient loses consciousness, bedside PG is declining too fast, or symptoms of severe hypoglycemia occur; also given if PG remains <55 mg/dL at 30 minutes or <60 mg/dL at 45 minutes post glucagon dose

studyInterventions.name: Acetaminophen (paracetamol)
studyInterventions.description: Permitted at investigator discretion for treatment of headaches; maximum 1 g per dose, maximum 2 g per 24 hours

studyInterventions.name: Basal insulin analogs
studyInterventions.description: Permitted stable background therapy; includes insulin glargine (U_100 or U_300) or insulin degludec (U_100); last basal injection no later than 12 hours prior to hypoglycemia induction procedure

studyInterventions.name: Rapid_acting insulin analogs
studyInterventions.description: Permitted stable background therapy; includes insulin lispro, insulin aspart, or insulin glulisine; last prandial injection no later than 6 hours prior to hypoglycemia induction procedure

studyInterventions.name: Oral anti_hyperglycemic medications (OAMs)
studyInterventions.description: Permitted stable background therapy for T2DM patients; includes metformin, DPP_4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors, sulfonylureas (not more than half of maximum approved dose), glinides, alpha_glucosidase inhibitors, or thiazolidines; last dose no later than 12 hours prior to hypoglycemia induction procedure

studyInterventions.name: Anti_hypertensive medications
studyInterventions.description: Permitted stable background therapy; must remain on stable regimen for at least 3 months; no change within 30 days prior to screening

studyInterventions.name: Anti_lipidemic medications
studyInterventions.description: Permitted stable background therapy; must remain on stable regimen for at least 3 months

studyInterventions.name: Pro_motility medications (e.g., metoclopramide, domperidone)
studyInterventions.description: Permitted during study but must be washed out at least 7 days before each treatment period and not taken while in the CRU

studyInterventions.name: Opiate medications (e.g., morphine)
studyInterventions.description: Permitted during study but must be washed out at least 7 days before each treatment period and not taken while in the CRU

studyInterventions.name: Medications with anti_emetic effects (e.g., promethazine, prochlorperazine)
studyInterventions.description: Permitted during study but must be washed out at least 7 days before each treatment period and not taken while in the CRU

studyInterventions.name: Beta_blockers
studyInterventions.description: Prohibited throughout the course of the study; daily systemic use excluded
